primary_topics: Unveiling and signing of the foundation stone marker for the PhilJA Development Center, November 30, 2006 -- CJP's second-to-last major ceremony as CJ (retires December 6, 2006)

The PhilJA Development Center journey: from the July 19, 1995 land transfer (Antonio Carpio as Presidential Legal Counsel to Ramos; 3.3 hectares); the November 23, 1998 first cornerstone under CJ Narvasa; CJ Davide's pursuit of Japanese funding; Ambassador Yamazaki's P300 million grant (January 26, 2006)

PhilJA's future vision: national and ASEAN regional hub for continuing judicial education; cooperation agreements with Spain and Egypt; pending agreements with France, UK, Russia and Pakistan; special school for career judges (Foreign Service Institute model)

ACID connection: PhilJA addresses the 'I' (incompetence) in ACID; 'the intensified campaign to eradicate the corrosive effects of ACID can be waged much faster and more successfully if we start at the very foundations of judicial training and education'
sub_topics: Foundation stone ceremony context: 'gathering of friends of the Center... persons who have been instrumental in bringing about, furthering and realizing our dream'

Journey timeline: July 19, 1995 -- at the instance of Presidential Legal Counsel Antonio T. Carpio, President Ramos turned over the 3.3-hectare facility to the SC; November 23, 1998 -- first cornerstone under CJ Narvasa; throughout CJ Davide's term -- pursued Japanese government funding; CJ Davide's request for funding finally granted through Ambassador Yamazaki's 'kind support and determined persistence'; January 26, 2006 -- Ambassador Yamazaki handed over the strings-free P300 million grant to the Philippine government and then to the SC

PhilJA's vision: 'first and only training school for the Philippine judiciary'; renovation and construction will make it 'comparable with other training institutions; national and, I hope, an ASEAN regional hub for continuing legal and judicial education, pre-judicature training, judicial career enhancement, and various programs in specialized areas of the law'
International cooperation: signed judicial education cooperation agreements with Spain and Egypt; firming up agreements with France, UK, Russia and Pakistan

Special school for judges: 'similar in concept and orientation to our very own Foreign Service Institute'; entrants pass battery of competitive examinations and interviews; 'only the best and the brightest will be trained for a career in the judiciary... professional judges who will not just be steeped in the law, but also be deep in ethical and moral values'

ACID connection: four Ins vow (independence, integrity, industry, intelligence); ACID problems (access, corruption, incompetence, delay); 'PhilJA as the primary education arm of the Supreme Court rightly deserve priority. After all, the intensified campaign to eradicate the corrosive effects of ACID can be waged much faster and more successfully if we start at the very foundations of judicial training and education.'
Closing: 'May I invite all of you to join hands with me in building the PhilJA Development Center, our chronicle of faith and our testament of hope for a reformed judiciary.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 30, 2006 at the unveiling and signing of the foundation stone marker for the PhilJA Development Center in Tagaytay -- six days before CJP's mandatory retirement -- this address recounts 'the long and tortuous journey... indeed a chronicle of faith.' The journey: July 19, 1995 -- at the instance of Presidential Legal Counsel Antonio T. Carpio, President Ramos turned over the 3.3-hectare facility to the SC; November 23, 1998 -- first cornerstone under CJ Narvasa; throughout CJ Davide's term -- pursued Japanese government funding; January 26, 2006 -- Ambassador Ryuichiro Yamazaki handed over the strings-free P300 million grant to the Philippine government and then to the SC. PhilJA is 'the first and only training school for the Philippine judiciary'; the completed Development Center will make it a national and 'ASEAN regional hub for continuing legal and judicial education, pre-judicature training, judicial career enhancement, and various programs in specialized areas of the law.' CJP has signed judicial education cooperation agreements with Spain and Egypt; agreements with France, UK, Russia and Pakistan are being finalized. Longer-term vision: a special school for young lawyers aspiring to become career judges -- 'similar in concept and orientation to our very own Foreign Service Institute'; competitive examinations to ensure 'only the best and the brightest are trained... professional judges who will not just be steeped in the law, but also be deep in ethical and moral values.' The ACID connection: 'the intensified campaign to eradicate the corrosive effects of ACID can be waged much faster and more successfully if we start at the very foundations of judicial training and education.' Closing: 'May I invite all of you to join hands with me in building the PhilJA Development Center, our chronicle of faith and our testament of hope for a reformed judiciary.'
